issues.legal_issue: A person whose possession derives from a decree-holder must restore possession when the decree under which the decree-holder obtained possession is set aside, even if that person claims to be a bona fide tenant.
material_facts: An ex parte eviction order enabled the landlord to obtain possession of the premises from the tenant.
After the eviction order was set aside and the eviction proceeding revived, the tenant sought restoration of possession.
Before restoration was carried out, another person objected, stating that the landlord had inducted him as a tenant and that he had acted bona fide without knowledge of the earlier proceeding.
The later occupant obtained possession from the landlord, rather than through an independent auction purchase.
issues.conclusion: The later occupant was required to restore possession because his possession derived from the landlord, who had obtained possession under the eviction order that was set aside. The tenant was entitled to restoration, subject to the result of the revived eviction proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires restitution when a decree or order is varied or reversed, including restoration of benefits obtained under it. A tenant inducted into possession by a decree-holder derives possession from that decree-holder and cannot claim the independent position of a stranger who purchases at an execution sale and was not a party to the decree. The Court applied Binayak Swain v. Ramesh Chandra Panigrahi, which approved the distinction stated in Zain-ul-Abdin Khan v. Muhammad Asghar Ali Khan between a decree-holder purchasing under a decree later reversed and a bona fide stranger purchasing at a valid execution sale.

predicates.restitution_after_reversal: A party seeks restoration of possession after the order under which possession was obtained has been set aside or reversed.
predicates.occupant_possession_derived_from_decree_: The current occupant obtained possession from the person who obtained it under the order that was set aside or reversed.
predicates.derivative_occupant_must_restore_possess: An occupant whose possession derives from the decree-holder must restore possession.

issues.definition: When restoration is sought after an order is set aside and the current occupant obtained possession from the person who gained possession under that order, the occupant must restore possession.
